recommendation_summary: The reply recommends wrapping the cron call on edna in a small shell script that always emails the user a one-line success or failure-with-exit-code message, even when the Python script crashes before its own email step.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You want to know within a day if nightly-sync fails, without having to read logs yourself.
labels.Deleted: Central log server and Docker on Synology — nobody asked for log aggregation, and since you've said you won't read logs anyway, a log store wouldn't even meet the requirement.
labels.Bottleneck: nightly-sync's email step never runs when it crashes at startup, so the only alert you have is silent exactly when you need it.
labels.Checked myself: Based only on what you told me — four silent crashes last week, no other alerting exists today, I haven't touched edna or the Synology this turn.

note: The reply recommends one email alert from a wrapper and rejects the log and Docker stack, though it would stay silent if cron never runs, and 'nobody asked for log aggregation' misstates the user's own proposal.
